name: Callisto from Voyager 1, March 6, 1979, 14:06 UTC
blurb: Jupiter's moon Callisto, about 4,820 kilometers across. Seen by Voyager 1's wide-angle camera through orange, green, blue and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: Callisto filling much of the frame, nearly fully lit, from about 210,000 kilometers away, 1 day after Voyager 1's closest approach to Jupiter on March 5, 1979. Its rocky, icy surface is the oldest and most heavily cratered in the solar system.
